document.title: Afghanistan: Foreign Secretary Mulls over Afghanistan (Islama 08637)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] Pakistan Foreign Secretary Najamuddin Shaikh insists Pakistani aid to the Taliban is not increasing and that Pakistan urges the Taliban to cooperate with other factions. Ambassador Simons says the U.S. will keep urging Pakistan not to side with the Taliban.

events.description: Foreign Secretary Shaikh called in US Ambassador to discuss Afghanistan.
Shaikh called Ambassador to say he found no basis for reports of increased Pakistani assistance to the Taliban.
Ambassador updated Shaikh on Taliban's decision to delay a US delegation visit.
Foreign Secretary Shaikh called in US Ambassador Simons to discuss Afghanistan, stressing that Pakistan is not siding with the Taliban and wants Taliban-Dostam talks.
Shaikh called the Ambassador to say he had checked and found no increase in Pakistani assistance to the Taliban.
The US DCM met a Taliban representative; the Taliban decided to delay a USG delegation visit until after recognition by some Islamic countries.
The Ambassador updated Shaikh on the status of the USG visit to Kabul.
Ijlal Zaidi led a Pakistani team to the three Central Asian states bordering Afghanistan to discuss developments.
Dostam's forces reportedly abandoned positions on the south side of the Salang Tunnel.

key_claims: Pakistan's Foreign Secretary denied that Pakistan was siding with the Taliban and said its aim was to bring the Taliban and Dostam together.
Shaikh dodged questions on increased Pakistani material support to the Taliban, later claiming he checked and found none.
Shaikh suggested ICRC convoys might be mistaken for Pakistani military vehicles.
Dostam reportedly abandoned Salang Tunnel positions and received arms from retreating Massoud and Hekmatyar forces.
The Taliban delayed a US delegation visit until recognition by some Islamic countries.
Shaikh judged Iran unlikely to unleash Ismail Khan, and said Iran was surprised by the Taliban's advance.
The US Ambassador would urge Pakistan not to side with the Taliban and to push national reconciliation.
